newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan frees opposition figure, he calls for change.
newsitem.headline: Sudan frees opposition figure, he calls for change.

text.p: A newly freed Sudanese political prisoner said on Thursday Sudan's civil war would continue unless the government was replaced.
"Unless the National Islamic Front (NIF) government is removed and substituted by a national government, there will be no peace," Sid Ahmed Hussein told Reuters in an interview.

The government of President Lt-General Omar Hassan Al-Bashir said on Tuesday it would free all political prisoners to "allow the chance for all political opponents inside and outside the country to reconsider their positions."
Hussein, the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) deputy secretary general and its senior remaining man in Sudan, was released on Wednesday after being detained since January.
Hussein said there were at least 250 political detainees in Sudan, including members of the "DUP, Umma Party, Communist party, trade unionists students and young people."
He said prominent detainees were treated well but those accused of working with Abdel Aziz Khalid, a leading member of the opposition's umbrella group National Democratic Alliance, were not.
"We saw traces of torture. On their backs were signs of beatings and their legs were burnt," he said.

Sudanese parliament speaker Hassan al-Turabi said in January Sudan had arrested up to 15 opposition party members after rebels in the south seized two towns on the Ethiopian border. He said the DUP and Umma Party members were held under a public security law.
Hussein said the NIF would have to accept democracy and a multi-party system and remove emergency laws before a change in its attitude to political opponents could be considered genuine.

"Since 1990, we have been in and out of detention. We have been watched in our houses and questioned. If the emergency laws are not removed, there is nothing to prevent them from coming tomorrow to take us again," Hussein said.
The present government seized power in 1989 and later banned political parties. Hussein was a deputy prime minister from 1986 to 1989 and also held other cabinet posts.

Rebels led by the Sudan People's Liberation Army have been fighting the Khartoum government since 1983. The government signed a peace deal in April with several groups formerly linked with the SPLA led by John Garang, who has vowed to keep fighting.
